title: Probe of fatal shooting upsets kin
article: The parents of an 18-year-old killed by police want some answers.
Keyvan Tabesh was shot by a Port Moody officer last July after he rushed the officer with a machete in his hand.
His family were told this week that prosecutors have decided not to charge the unnamed officer who shot Tabesh.

"How can we accept an investigation that the Port Moody Police Department has done when the shooter was one of their own officers?" Tabesh's mother Forough Tabesh asked yesterday. "There should be an independent investigation."
Geoffrey Gaul, director of legal services for the prosecution, said: "We were of the opinion that the officer was justified in using the amount of force he did under the circumstances."

Police said at the time that Tabesh, who was known to police but had no record, had repeatedly struck a vehicle with a machete before speeding off in a car. The plainclothes police officer followed it into a cul-de-sac where the shooting occurred.
Amir Aghaei, who was in the car with Tabesh, also approached the officer and was wounded.
Forough said the family wants details of what happened at the shooting. She said prosecutors did not share information about it with them.
"We asked for a copy of the investigation but they would not give it to us," she said.
Lawyer Don Morrison has filed notice of a civil suit against the City of Port Moody and has taken the first steps in launching a complaint through the police complaint process.
"The family operates in a vacuum," Morrison said. "They've had a very tragic event happen in their lives. They seek information and at every turn they are stonewalled."
Coroner Liana Wright said she will set a date for an inquest now that there will be no charges.
Forough Tabesh added: "We know nothing can bring Keyvan back, but we want to know why he died."
